content: Aristotle (384–322 BCE) was an ancient Greek philosopher, student of Plato, and tutor of Alexander the Great, who made foundational contributions to logic, metaphysics, ethics, politics, biology, and scientific thought, shaping Western philosophy with his empirical approach and systematic analysis of reality.
